title: Harnessing the healing power of music, with Renée Fleming and Aniruddh Patel, PhD

sentences.en: For centuries, people have used music to soothe and to heal, but it's only in recent decades
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，人们一直用音乐来舒缓身心、疗愈伤痛，但直到近几十年

sentences.en: that scientists have begun to study and understand how music affects our minds and our bodies.
sentences.zh: 科学家才开始研究并理解音乐是如何影响我们的心灵与身体的。

sentences.en: Armed with new research tools, scientists have been learning more about how our brains process music and exploring how music can be used to improve health and well-being in
sentences.zh: 借助全新的研究工具，科学家们不仅对我们的大脑如何处理音乐有了更深入的了解，还在探索如何利用音乐来改善健康与福祉，

sentences.en: areas as diverse as chronic pain, Parkinson's disease, and stroke recovery.
sentences.zh: 涉及的领域广泛，包括慢性疼痛、帕金森病和中风康复等。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk about this latest research in the field with a world-renowned musician who has become a leading proponent of research on the connection between music,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与一位世界知名的音乐家——她已成为连接音乐、

sentences.en: the arts, and health, and a scientist who studies the cognition and evolutionary origins of music.
sentences.zh: 艺术与健康研究的领军人物，以及一位研究音乐认知与演化起源的科学家，共同探讨该领域的最新研究成果。

sentences.en: Some of the questions we hope to tackle are, did humans evolve to be an inherently musical species?
sentences.zh: 我们希望探讨的一些问题包括：人类在演化上是否天生就是一个具有音乐性的物种？

sentences.en: How can understanding the evolutionary origins of music help us develop more effective music therapies?
sentences.zh: 理解音乐的演化起源如何能帮助我们开发出更有效的音乐疗法？

sentences.en: What are some of the music therapies being used today?
sentences.zh: 当今正在使用的是哪些音乐疗法？

sentences.en: What are the biggest challenges remaining in the field?
sentences.zh: 该领域目前还存在哪些最大的挑战？

sentences.en: And what is the most promising research direction for the future?
sentences.zh: 未来最有前景的研究方向是什么？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客节目，主要探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: As I said, we have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 如我所说，我们今天请到了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: The first will need no introduction for music lovers.
sentences.zh: 对于音乐爱好者来说，第一位嘉宾无需过多介绍。

sentences.en: Soprano Renee Fleming is one of the most celebrated musicians of our time, sometimes called the people's diva.
sentences.zh: 女高音歌唱家蕾妮·弗莱明是我们时代最负盛名的音乐家之一，有时被称为“人民的迪瓦”。

sentences.en: She's performed on the world's leading opera stages and concert halls and appeared with all the major orchestras of Europe and North America.
sentences.zh: 她曾在世界顶级的歌剧院和音乐厅演出，并与欧洲和北美的各大交响乐团合作过。

sentences.en: Among her many awards are the
sentences.zh: 在她的众多荣誉中，包括

sentences.en: National Medal of the Arts and five Grammys.
sentences.zh: 国家艺术勋章和五项格莱美奖。

sentences.en: In recent years, she's become a leading advocate for research on the science of music and how the arts can be used in health and healing.
sentences.zh: 近年来，她成为了音乐科学研究以及如何将艺术用于健康与疗愈的倡导者。

sentences.en: As artistic advisor to the John F.
sentences.zh: 作为约翰·F·

sentences.en: Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, she leads the Sound Health Initiative in partnership with the National Institutes of Health and the National Endowment for the Arts.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪表演艺术中心的艺术顾问，她与美国国立卫生研究院和国家艺术基金会合作，领导了“声音健康计划”。

sentences.en: She's given presentations with scientists and practitioners around the world and is editor of a new book called
sentences.zh: 她曾与世界各地的科学家和从业者进行过演讲，并是一本名为

sentences.en: Music and Mind, Harnessing the Arts for Health and Wellness, which includes contributions from eminent
sentences.zh: 《音乐与心灵：利用艺术促进健康与福祉》的新书的主编，该书汇集了杰出的

sentences.en: scientists, musicians, and other artists on the intersection of science, health, music, and art.
sentences.zh: 科学家、音乐家和其他艺术家关于科学、健康、音乐和艺术交汇点的撰文。

sentences.en: My second guest is one of the contributors to this book.
sentences.zh: 我的第二位嘉宾正是这本书的撰稿人之一。

sentences.en: Dr. Anarutz Patel is a professor of psychology at Tufts University, where he researches the cognitive, neural, and evolutionary foundations of musicality.
sentences.zh: 阿纳鲁茨·帕特尔博士是塔夫茨大学的心理学教授，他在那里研究音乐性的认知、神经和演化基础。

sentences.en: Most recently, he's been studying how other animals process music as a window into how human musicality evolved.
sentences.zh: 最近，他一直在研究其他动物如何处理音乐，以此作为窗口来了解人类音乐性是如何演化而来的。

sentences.en: He's author of the 2008 book Music, Language, and the Brain, which won the ASCAP
sentences.zh: 他是2008年出版的《音乐、语言与大脑》一书的作者，该书曾荣获ASCAP

sentences.en: Deems Taylor Award and is working on a new book about the evolution of human musicality to be published by Princeton University Press.
sentences.zh: 迪姆斯·泰勒奖，目前他正在撰写一本关于人类音乐性演化的新书，将由普林斯顿大学出版社出版。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位做客我的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Now, Renee, if I may call you by your first name.
sentences.zh: 蕾妮，如果我直接叫你的名字，可以吗？

sentences.en: Yes, please.
sentences.zh: 可以，请吧。

sentences.en: Let's start with you.
sentences.zh: 我们先从你开始聊起。

sentences.en: How did you first become interested in the connection between music and health and the brain?
sentences.zh: 你是如何开始对音乐、健康与大脑之间的联系产生兴趣的？

sentences.en: What led you to do this work and put this book together?
sentences.zh: 是什么促使你开展这项工作并把这本书汇编在一起的？

sentences.en: Well, I had performing anxiety that manifested in unusual ways, and one of them was pain.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我曾患有表演焦虑，这种焦虑以不寻常的方式表现出来，其中之一就是疼痛。

sentences.en: So, pain was a distraction from the performance anxiety, from the pressure of performance.
sentences.zh: 所以，疼痛转移了我对表演焦虑的注意力，缓解了表演带来的压力。

sentences.en: I was not an innate or natural performer at all.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不是一个天生或自然的表演者。

sentences.en: I love music, and I loved studying music and being in a practice room, but I wasn't kind of a gregarious, outgoing kid.
sentences.zh: 我热爱音乐，喜欢学习音乐并在练功房里练习，但我并不是那种热情外向的孩子。

sentences.en: And so, in trying to figure that out, I did a lot of reading on the mind-body connection.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了弄清楚这一点，我阅读了大量关于身心联系的书籍。

sentences.en: Dr. Sona, his work was very helpful to me.
sentences.zh: 索纳博士的工作对我有很大帮助。

sentences.en: And along the way, I discovered that researchers were studying music.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，我发现研究人员正在研究音乐。

sentences.en: And when I met Dr. Francis Collins at a dinner party in 2015, I asked him why.
sentences.zh: 2015年，我在一次晚宴上遇到了弗朗西斯·柯林斯博士，我问他为什么。

sentences.en: And because I had just been appointed advisor to the Kennedy Center, I said, do you think the NIH and the Kennedy Center could
sentences.zh: 因为我刚被任命为肯尼迪中心的顾问，我说，你认为国立卫生研究院和肯尼迪中心能否

sentences.en: work together to provide a platform for science with the public?
sentences.zh: 合作，为公众的科学研究提供一个平台？

sentences.en: Because I think the public would be as interested as I am in the work that's happening at this intersection of health and art.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为公众会和我一样对健康与艺术交汇处正在发生的工作感兴趣。

sentences.en: And he said yes, and we've been passionately sharing this information ever since.
sentences.zh: 他说可以，从那以后，我们就一直充满热情地分享这些信息。

sentences.en: Dr. Patel, is it okay if I call you, Ani?
sentences.zh: 帕特尔博士，我叫你阿尼，可以吗？

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 请吧。

sentences.en: Your chapter of the book is called, Are We an Inherently Musical Species?
sentences.zh: 你在书中的章节题为《我们是天生具有音乐性的物种吗？》。

sentences.en: Can you talk about what it means to be an inherently musical species, and why this is an important question to ask?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈成为一个天生具有音乐性的物种意味着什么，以及为什么这是一个重要的问题吗？

sentences.en: So, this is one of the big questions about human nature that's unresolved, and where there are major thinkers on taking opposite viewpoints.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于人类天性但尚未解决的重大问题，在这个问题上，思想家们持有截然相反的观点。

sentences.en: So, Charles Darwin, in his book on human evolution, about 150 years ago, argued that we are inherently musical.
sentences.zh: 因此，查尔斯·达尔文大约150年前在他的关于人类演化的书中提出，我们是天生具有音乐性的。

sentences.en: We are musical today because our ancestors evolved musical behavior, which had some functional value for our ancestors, and that laid the foundation for our musicality today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天之所以有音乐性，是因为我们的祖先演化出了音乐行为，这为我们的祖先带来了一些功能价值，从而为我们今天的音乐性奠定了基础。

sentences.en: William James, his contemporary, very much disagreed, and he loved music.
sentences.zh: 他的同时代人威廉·詹姆斯对此非常不赞同，尽管他很喜欢音乐。

sentences.en: He loved Darwin, but he thought music was a purely cultural invention, something that we were fortunate to
sentences.zh: 他很崇拜达尔文，但他认为音乐纯粹是一种文化发明，是我们很幸运地

sentences.en: figure out how to do and enriches human life, but not something we specifically evolved to do.
sentences.zh: 弄清楚如何去做并丰富了人类生活的事物，而不是我们为了特定目的演化出来的事情。

sentences.en: And perhaps I can give you an analogy to help clarify the difference.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以举个类比来帮助阐明这种区别。

sentences.en: Neuroscientists today completely agree that we evolved to speak and use language.
sentences.zh: 今天的神经科学家完全一致认为，我们演化出了说话和使用语言的能力。

sentences.en: Our brains have specialized circuits for that, an ability that is part of our human nature.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑有专门的回路，这种能力是我们人类天性的一部分。

sentences.en: We have to learn it.
sentences.zh: 我们必须去学习它。

sentences.en: Babies have to learn how to speak, but we have predisposed to learn that skill by evolutionary biology.
sentences.zh: 婴儿必须学会如何说话，但我们在演化生物学上就预设了学习这种技能的倾向。

sentences.en: They also agree that we didn't evolve to read and write.
sentences.zh: 他们也一致认为，我们并没有演化出读写能力。

sentences.en: Reading and writing is a purely cultural invention.
sentences.zh: 读写能力纯粹是一种文化发明。

sentences.en: It takes advantage of the fact that we have language, that we have good visual perception and good attention and good motor control.
sentences.zh: 它利用了我们拥有语言、良好的视觉感知、良好的注意力和良好的运动控制这一事实。

sentences.en: And we put all those things together to create written language, which is a hugely important part of our life.
sentences.zh: 我们将所有这些东西结合在一起创造了书面语言，这是我们生活中极其重要的一部分。

sentences.en: Nobody would dispute that language writing is enormously valuable to our society and our culture.
sentences.zh: 没有人会否认文字书写对我们的社会和文化具有巨大的价值。

sentences.en: And so it's not a question about the value of music.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是一个关于音乐价值的问题。

sentences.en: If music is a purely cultural invention like writing, it could still be very valuable for health, for culture, for social reasons, but not something we specifically evolved to do.
sentences.zh: 如果音乐纯粹像写作一样是一种文化发明，它对健康、文化、社会原因仍然可能非常有价值，但并不是我们专门为了做而演化出来的东西。

sentences.en: So I think it's an important question because it's unresolved.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一个重要的问题，因为它尚未解决。

sentences.en: And also because we're finally at a turning point where after 150 years, we might be able to
sentences.zh: 而且这也是因为我们终于来到了一个转折点，在经历150年之后，我们或许能够

sentences.en: start to answer this question with science using data from fields like brain imaging, genetics, studies
sentences.zh: 开始用科学来回答这个问题，利用来自脑成像、遗传学等领域的

sentences.en: of other species, studies of child development, studies of cross-cultural studies, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 其他物种研究、儿童发展研究、跨文化研究等的数据。

sentences.en: And so it's exciting time to be studying this question.
sentences.zh: 所以现在研究这个问题是一个令人兴奋的时刻。

sentences.en: To follow up, your recent research has tried to answer the question about musicality by looking at musicality and other species, including dogs and parrots.
sentences.zh: 作为跟进，你最近的研究试图通过观察包括狗和鹦鹉在内的其他物种的音乐性来回答关于音乐性的问题。

sentences.en: What can we learn about music and humans by studying other animals?
sentences.zh: 通过研究其他动物，我们能了解关于音乐和人类的什么信息？

sentences.en: One thing we can learn is to some extent, we don't have a time machine.
sentences.zh: 我们可以学到的一点是，在某种程度上，我们没有时间机器。

sentences.en: We can't go back and figure out how music began in our species.
sentences.zh: 我们无法回到过去，去弄清楚音乐在我们这个物种中是如何开始的。

sentences.en: So what comparative biologists do, evolutionary biologists, we look at other species to get clues.
sentences.zh: 所以比较生物学家、演化生物学家会通过观察其他物种来寻找线索。

sentences.en: So for example, take beat, our sense of beat in music, which is something we see all over the world.
sentences.zh: 比如，以节拍为例，我们在音乐中感受到的节拍感，这是我们在世界各地都能看到的现象。

sentences.en: Every culture has some form of music with a beat.
sentences.zh: 每种文化都有某种带节拍的音乐形式。

sentences.en: Often people use it for dancing and so forth.
sentences.zh: 人们经常用它来跳舞等等。

sentences.en: And children learn how to move to a beat and synchronize their movements to a beat without any special instruction.
sentences.zh: 孩子们无需经过专门的指导，就能学会随着节拍运动并将动作与节拍同步。

sentences.en: They pick it up from watching others and socializing and so forth.
sentences.zh: 他们通过观察他人、社交等方式学会了这一点。

sentences.en: And for many people, this is the most primal aspect of music.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这是音乐中最原始的方面。

sentences.en: And they think, okay, if there's one aspect of music that we might share with other animals, it's going to be beat and our sense of beat and our ability to move to the beat.
sentences.zh: 他们会想，好吧，如果说音乐有什么方面是我们可能与其他动物共享的，那一定就是节拍、我们的节拍感以及随着节拍运动的能力。

sentences.en: Well, actually it turns out that our closest living relatives, apes and monkeys, don't seem to have a sense of beat like we do.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，结果证明，我们现存最近的亲属——类人猿和猴子，似乎并不具备像我们这样的节拍感。

sentences.en: They don't seem to synchronize to beat spontaneously when they hear beat-based rhythms, when you try to train them.
sentences.zh: 当你给它们播放基于节拍的节奏或者试图训练它们时，它们似乎不会自发地与节拍同步。

sentences.en: Monkeys do it very differently.
sentences.zh: 猴子的做法非常不同。

sentences.en: A fundamental aspect of how we deal with beat is we predict the beat.
sentences.zh: 我们处理节拍的一个基本方面就是预测节拍。

sentences.en: When you perceive a beat, you automatically start to predict when the next beat is coming very accurately.
sentences.zh: 当你感知到一个节拍时，你会自动开始非常准确地预测下一个节拍什么时候到来。

sentences.en: And that's how you can clap right on time or dance right on time with a beat.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你能随着节拍准时鼓掌或准时跳舞。

sentences.en: If you try to train a monkey to tap to a beat, they wait for the beat and then they react.
sentences.zh: 如果你试图训练一只猴子随着节拍敲击，它们会等待节拍然后做出反应。

sentences.en: They don't predict.
sentences.zh: 它们不会去预测。

sentences.en: And it takes a lot of special training to get them to predict.
sentences.zh: 并且需要进行大量专门的训练才能让它们学会预测。

sentences.en: So their brains just deal with beat in a very different way.
sentences.zh: 所以它们的大脑处理节拍的方式非常不同。

sentences.en: So why do we have this ability that seems so simple and yet is not shared with our close living relatives?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们拥有这种看起来如此简单却又没有与我们现存近亲共享的能力呢？

sentences.en: Usually biological things that are simple are shared, like the way a kidney works, or I'm not saying the kidney is simple, but there's a lot of shared biology between us and our
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，简单的生物学特征是共享的，比如肾脏的工作方式，或者我并不是说肾脏很简单，但是我们与

sentences.en: close cousins and shared things like visual perception abilities.
sentences.zh: 近亲之间有很多共享的生物学特征以及像视觉感知能力这样共享的东西。

sentences.en: I theorized at one point that maybe there's something about only certain kinds of animal brains can acquire this ability spontaneously to move to a beat.
sentences.zh: 我曾一度推测，也许只有特定种类的动物大脑才能具备这种自发随着节拍运动的能力。

sentences.en: And those are brains that have the ability to learn complex sounds to what's called complex vocal learning.
sentences.zh: 这些大脑具备学习复杂声音的能力，也就是所谓的复杂声乐学习能力。

sentences.en: Listening and imitating sounds is how you acquire your sound repertoire.
sentences.zh: 倾听并模仿声音是你获取声音库的方式。

sentences.en: And that's a rare ability.
sentences.zh: 这是一种罕见的能力。

sentences.en: We're the only primate with that ability.
sentences.zh: 我们是唯一具备这种能力的灵长类动物。

sentences.en: Dogs don't have it.
sentences.zh: 狗没有。

sentences.en: Cats don't have it.
sentences.zh: 猫没有。

sentences.en: The vast majority of animals don't have it.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数动物都没有。

sentences.en: But there's a group of animals, three groups of birds that have it, songbirds, hummingbirds, and parrots.
sentences.zh: 但有一组动物，也就是三类鸟类具备这种能力，即鸣禽、蜂鸟和鹦鹉。

sentences.en: And we showed that, so I hypothesized that maybe this ability helped lay the foundation for beat synchronization.
sentences.zh: 我们证明了这一点，所以我假设这种能力可能为节拍同步奠定了基础。

sentences.en: And then we showed that actually a parrot could actually spontaneously move to the beat of music and keep the beat at different tempi that was replicated by another group.
sentences.zh: 然后我们证明了实际上鹦鹉可以自发地随着音乐的节拍运动，并在不同的节奏下保持节拍，这一发现在另一个研究小组中得到了重复。

sentences.en: And so now it looks like they're the only other species besides humans that do this spontaneously, which gives us some clues about the origin of this ability in our own evolution.
sentences.zh: 所以现在看来，它们是除了人类之外唯一能自发做到这一点的物种，这为我们了解这种能力在我们自身演化过程中的起源提供了一些线索。

sentences.en: It seems like perhaps the ability to imitate complex sounds was one of the foundations from which beat synchronization emerged.
sentences.zh: 似乎模仿复杂声音的能力可能是节拍同步从中涌现的基础之一。

sentences.en: So it's kind of a way of going back in time and thinking about what were the precursors to this ability in our own evolution without having a time machine.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是一种回到过去的方式，在没有时间机器的情况下，去思考在我们自己的演化中这种能力的先驱是什么。

sentences.en: I want to talk more about animals at some point.
